correctness.rationale: Given k,n>0 and N in L1_loc(I), test the PDE h_t=k∂x(h∂xh)+v_s ∂x h−φh+N(t)/n in any compactly supported test function in U×I. Because h=0 locally there, all distributional derivatives of h and the local nonlinear flux vanish, leaving N(t)/n=0 as a distribution on I after using a spatial test with nonzero integral; n>0 gives N(t)=0 almost everywhere. The proof is independent of contact/interface delta terms because tests are supported strictly away from the moving edge. It makes no assertion where the PDE is posed only on saturated/wet points.
residual_risks: Product h ∂x h is interpreted locally in the weak solution class; locally identically zero implies zero local flux under standard distributional PDE assumptions.
A dry interval may move; claim assumes one fixed open cylinder in space-time, and does not assert existence after wetting fronts vanish.

originality.rationale: The full Bartlett–Porporato (2018) article derives a time-only additive N(t) in its source term and assigns zero water height beyond sharp wetting fronts, but also frames the conservation law as flow *within the saturated zone*. It does not explicitly state the full-line distributional no-source compatibility of the extension. General porous-medium finite propagation and local support lemmas are standard; no originality is claimed for distributional calculus itself. The new finding is a clearly conditional, model-specific clarification of when the printed source and zero extension can be interpreted together. Priority claim is deliberately narrow.
residual_risks: The source may intentionally impose its Boussinesq equation only in the saturated region; then the observation corrects only a possible *full-line* reading, not the original interior solution.
The local dry-set test is a standard distribution principle; the new content is the explicit application and interpretation, not an independent PDE theorem.

value.rationale: The underlying paper explicitly offers varying recharge/sink terms and sharp finite wetting fronts as a weak solution; whether its source persists in dry ground changes the mathematical validity of the advertised zero extension. The dry-cylinder test gives an exact, actionable necessary condition that distinguishes full-line weak formulations from wet-domain/localized-source formulations. It is a short local argument, but the model-specific interpretation is substantive for correct use of the source-driven aquifer profile; no broad new porous-medium theory is claimed.
residual_risks: The source may consistently intend a saturated-region-only PDE, in which case this observation is a clarification, not a discovered physical inconsistency.
No existence/uniqueness or accuracy of an alternative model is established.

final_claim: If the printed Boussinesq PDE with spatially uniform additive N(t)/n is interpreted as a full-line distributional equation and its solution is identically zero on a fixed open dry cylinder U×I, then N(t)=0 almost everywhere on I.
limitations: Conditional on full-line distributional PDE semantics and a fixed dry cylinder; wet-region-only models not excluded.
